title: Sublimation Uniforms (2026)
verdict: For sublimation uniforms in 2026, Wooter is our first choice. Its custom uniforms are fully sublimated, which means any color and any pattern at the same price, with names, numbers and logos dyed into the fabric.

Boombah is the other direct maker, sublimating in its own factories. Champro's Juice line is cut-and-sew sublimation sold through dealers. Custom Ink resells sublimated lines from other brands. Nike Team offers build-to-order uniforms through dealers.

ranking.lacks: About three weeks, because every piece is printed and sewn to order.

why: Sublimation prints a design onto paper, then uses heat to turn the ink into gas that bonds with polyester fibers. The color ends up inside the fabric, not on it.

That has three consequences. The print cannot crack, peel or fade the way a heat-pressed number does. Any number of colors costs the same. And the fabric stays breathable because nothing sits on its surface.
The limits: it works on polyester, not cotton, and each piece is made to order, so there is a lead time.

faq.a: A polyester uniform whose design is dyed into the fabric with heat, so it is permanent.

faq.q: Is sublimation better than screen printing?
faq.a: For team uniforms, usually. It lasts longer and allows unlimited colors. Screen printing suits cotton and very simple designs.
Not under normal washing. Avoid bleach and high heat.

faq.q: What is the difference between sublimated and tackle twill?
faq.a: Tackle twill is fabric lettering sewn on, heavier and traditional. Sublimation is printed in and lighter.

faq.q: How long do sublimation uniforms take?
faq.a: Wooter averages three weeks from design approval. A one to two week rush is available for an added fee.
